name: Speech-Act Adverbial
pattern: supplementary adverbial oriented to the utterance act

entry.name: Speech-Act Adverbial
entry.pattern: supplementary adverbial oriented to the utterance act

1.definition: Characterizes the speaker’s manner or purpose in making the utterance.

projection.target: Frankly characterizes the speaker’s statement, not the repair's manner of failing. A paraphrase can mention speaking frankly without changing the content asserted.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Words about how you're speaking
curious.summary: An adverb like frankly can describe how or why the speaker is making the statement, not what the statement is about.
curious.body: In Frankly, the repair won't last, the word frankly isn't about the repair. It describes the speaker's way of speaking: the speaker is being frank in saying this. You can check by paraphrase. Something like I'm speaking frankly captures it, and the content asserted stays the same: the repair won't last. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional.
curious.try: Add a word like honestly or briefly to the start of a statement. Is it about the thing you're describing, or about how you're saying it?

teacher.summary: Helps explain an adverbial that characterizes the speaker's manner or purpose in making the utterance.
teacher.explain: A speech-act adverbial is a supplementary adverbial oriented to the utterance act: it characterizes the speaker's manner or purpose in making the utterance. In Frankly, the repair won't last, frankly characterizes the speaker's statement, not the repair's manner of failing. A paraphrase can mention speaking frankly without changing the content asserted. This dictionary relates it to evaluative sentence adverbs and to participial clause supplements. The analysis is marked provisional.
watch_for: A learner might read frankly as describing how the repair fails, when it describes the speaker's statement.
A learner might think the adverb changes the content asserted, when a paraphrase like I'm speaking frankly leaves it unchanged.
teacher.activity: Write statements with a speech-act adverb on cards. Students paraphrase each as I'm saying this ..., and check that the asserted content doesn't change.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Speech-Act Adverbial." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/speech-act-adverbial-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
